title: mcp dependency pinned >=2.3 with non-standard import paths
evidence: requirements.txt:1 pins `mcp>=2.3` (the published MCP Python SDK is 1.x); server.py:22-24 imports `from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer` and `from mcp_types import CallToolResult, TextContent`, which are not the standard SDK paths (`mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP`, `mcp.types`). Tests passed in retort's environment, so those symbols resolve there, but the project would not install/run against a stock PyPI `mcp`.
suggestion: Pin to a real published version and use the standard `mcp.server.fastmcp` / `mcp.types` import paths for portability.

title: Line coverage (56%) understates real coverage; server/knowledge run in subprocess
evidence: scores.json test_coverage=0.56; .coverage reports TOTAL 55.55% with server.py and knowledge.py at 0 in-process executed lines because the acceptance tests launch the server as a subprocess over MCP stdio (tests/acceptance/drivers/mcp_client.py:388-391, soccer_server_command at :466). Those modules are exercised end-to-end but not measured by in-process coverage.
suggestion: Enable subprocess coverage (coverage.process_startup / COVERAGE_PROCESS_START) if an accurate coverage number is wanted; behaviourally the code is covered by the 111 passing acceptance tests.

title: Acceptance tests verify the real MCP protocol over stdio
evidence: tests/acceptance/drivers/mcp_client.py implements a hand-rolled JSON-RPC stdio client (initialize handshake at :395-400, tools/call at :405-406) that spawns `python -m brazilian_soccer_mcp` as a subprocess, so R1 (MCP server) is verified against the wire protocol rather than by calling Python functions directly.
suggestion: None — this is a strength; noted for cross-run comparison.

title: 18 MCP tools exposed, exceeding the required query categories
evidence: server.py:47-159 registers find_matches, head_to_head, team_record, team_competitions, club_profile, league_table, top_scoring_teams, knockout_bracket, competition_summary, compare_seasons, biggest_wins, best_records, find_derbies, search_players, player_profile, brazilian_players_by_club and dataset_overview — covering all 5 spec capability groups plus extras (derbies, knockout brackets, season comparison).

title: Four-layer ATDD architecture (specs / DSL / drivers) with functional isolation
evidence: tests/acceptance/dsl/ (SoccerDsl, given, queries) sits above tests/acceptance/drivers/ (soccer_server, datasets, mcp_client); conftest.py:23-35 gives each spec its own tmp data dir and server instance (the `soccer` fixture) plus a shared read-only `provided` server over data/kaggle, matching Dave Farley's ATDD separation of what-from-how.
suggestion: None — matches the atdd-skill prompt's intent; atdd_review scored 0.9643.
